rationale: PINS the Matrix 1b parameters payload for groovy (#383 item 3 — cell PENDING -> #383). Groovy semantics: method symbols carry a parameters list with each parameter's name and declared type; varargs (String... parts) are modeled as an array type String[] per the JVM erasure convention (matching the java analyzer). M60 R10 FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-23): the first half of that rationale was FALSE for a qualified type. `Outer.Criterion` is the grammar's `scoped_type_identifier` (probe-verified against the pinned wasm), and this extractor's node list was the ONE place in the lane that did not accept it — the record-component extractor, the instantiation type node, and `baseTypeName`'s own doctrine ("a scoped type keeps its full dotted text, matching the Java analyzer convention") all already did. So a WRITTEN type was dropped from the payload while its declaration named it, and the override signature keyed on parameter types lost the distinction between two overloads differing only in a qualified type — the same 'a written name missing from the payload' class the lane's other extractors had already been fixed for. Measured before the fix on a 600-file grails-core sample (script/m60/groovy-parameter-payload-census.ts, joins by name+arity because a name-only join across groovy's heavy overloading reported 640 artifacts from 37 declarations): 8 of 33 joined written-qualified slots recorded no type. After the fix: 0 of 33, and the sample's untyped-parameter count falls 103 -> 66 — exactly the 37 written-qualified parameters, leaving the 66 genuinely dynamic `def`-style parameters honest. Every shape is pinned below: an interface method, its implementation, a CONSTRUCTOR parameter, a SPREAD (varargs) parameter, and the generic+qualified combination (`java.util.Map.Entry<String, Boolean>`), which was already accepted and must keep working.
